title: Stochastic bilevel gradients with two-point coupling within one fresh sample
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

task.detail: min_x Phi(x)=f(x,y*(x)); unique unconstrained global lower minimizer.
description_paragraphs: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

model.regularity: g(x,.) is mu_y-strongly convex; f,g have jointly L_f,L_g-Lipschitz gradients; ||grad_y f||<=C_f; g_{xy},g_{yy} are jointly rho-Lipschitz.
model.initialization: Phi(x0)-inf Phi<=Delta; ||y0-y*(x0)||<=R_y; initialize the two tracked lower iterates at the same y0.
model.stochastic_model: Conditional unbiasedness and bounded variances sigma_f^2,sigma_g^2 globally. Same-sample lower gradient obeys E||G_g(x,y1;xi)-G_g(x,y2;xi)||^2<=L_ms^2||y1-y2||^2 if L_ms<infinity; L_ms=infinity imposes no such smoothness.
model.scope: The MSS condition is in y at fixed x and on the full lower gradient; it does not assert full (x,y) MSS or sample-wise SC.
description_paragraphs:
The function $g(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex. The functions $
abla f,
abla g$ are jointly $L_f,L_g$-Lipschitz; $\|
abla_yf\|\le C_f$, and $g_{xy},g_{yy}$ is jointly $ho$-Lipschitz. Also $\Phi(x_0)-\inf\Phi\le\Delta$ and $\|y_0-y^*(x_0)\|\le R_y$.

Population gradients are unbiased, with variances bounded by $\sigma_f^2,\sigma_g^2$. If $L_{\mathrm{ms}}<\infty$, additionally require the common-sample condition $\mathbb{E}\|G_g(x,y_1;\xi)-G_g(x,y_2;\xi)\|^2\le L_{\mathrm{ms}}^2\|y_1-y_2\|^2$; $L_{\mathrm{ms}}=\infty$ means this condition is absent. It applies only in the lower-variable direction at fixed $x$.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

operations: Before a fresh draw choose at most two points z1,z2. Draw independent upper/lower sample seeds zeta,xi; return (G_f(z_j;zeta),G_g(z_j;xi)) for each requested point.
oracle.query_domain: All Euclidean points; both points are chosen before the draw.
oracle.coupling: Samples may be shared within this simultaneous batch only; they are not a reusable persistent sample handle. No informative y*-estimate is supplied (the r=infinity source specialization).
description_paragraphs: The algorithm specifies at most two points $z_1,z_2$ before sampling. Independent upper- and lower-level seeds $\zeta$ and $\xi$ are then drawn, and the oracle returns $(G_f(z_j;\zeta),G_g(z_j;\xi))$ at each requested point. The two points share the current batch seeds; different batches use fresh seeds. No persistent sample handle is provided.
Queries may use the full Euclidean space. Budgets, dimensions, and initial points are public. No additional localization information about $y^*(x)$ is supplied.
Return any measurable $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, possibly an unqueried point.

resource.projection: Q counts each actual point/sample gradient separately; two points and two functions cost four. Fixed batch size two makes this a constant-factor mapping of the source N-simultaneous interface.
resource.budget: Fixed outer/inner horizons and batches; all initialization and inner calls included.
description_paragraphs: Each function-point-sample gradient evaluation costs one unit. Querying both levels at two points costs four units. The fixed worst-case budget includes all inner, outer, and initialization calls.

Arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms are allowed, but both points in a batch must be fixed before its seed is drawn. Queries, stopping, and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable functions; outputs may be unqueried, randomly selected historical points, or admissible averages. No span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Queries are sequential, and each response in a batch is charged. Internal arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage are free; internal work, memory, and communication are not budgeted.
For every instance, $\mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$, with expectation over all randomness.
